Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Kim (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (Redwood CSM); Oliver Shaw (Bramble Ops Head of Platform), Priya Menon (SRE), Noah Herrera (ML Engineer), Aisha Khan (Security)

Summary: quick intro, objective to validate whether Redwood hosted or dedicated/private makes sense for Bramble's real-time chat and batch embedding workloads, capture p95 targets and define a benchmark.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, we brought Ethan our latency nerd and Lina on the CSM side; quick round robin?
[00:10] Oliver (Bramble): Oliver here, head of platform; main ask: we run a live chat product that needs token-by-token streaming with tight p95s, and a nightly batch embed job for search. We're trying to decide hosted vs reserved.
[00:22] Priya: hi, priya sres; we're worried about p95 spikes during promo events and slow tails around 99th percentiles, want a plan to handle sustained concurrency.
[00:35] Ethan (Redwood): great, can you tell us target p95s you're aiming for and expected concurrent streams / tokens per second?
[00:44] Noah: for chat UX we want perceived latency under 300ms p95 for first token (for streaming). For full response p95 ideally <1s for short replies (~40-80 tokens). Average traffic is 1200 reqs/minute but during peak we see bursts up to 7k reqs/minute and about 200 concurrent open streams.
[01:05] Maya: ok so 200 concurrent streaming sessions at peak, and 7k rps-ish burst, noted. Do you have a token/sec distribution or prompt length hist?
[01:15] Oliver: we can share a CSV, most sessions are multi-turn, avg prompt 60 tokens, model we're currently evaluating is a 7B-ish open model quantized.
[01:28] Ethan: helpful. A few quick clarifiers — when you say streaming p95 300ms for first token, is that from your app right of the wire to first token displayed, or from our API response start?
[01:38] Priya: from our app, so network + edge + inference. We can isolate layers but want to treat the inference slab as the main variable.
[01:46] Ethan: perfect. For that goal we usually look at continuous batching and KV cache warmness. Hosted can hit low latency if you use the small-hosted variant and streaming-optimized kernels, but the predictable tail for big bursts often benefits from Dedicated with reserved GPU pools or a private VPC if your compliance needs require it.
[02:06] Maya: also worth noting that prefix caching and sticky routing reduce p95 by avoiding cold KV population. That said, Dedicated gives you more isolation to avoid noisy neighbors during promos.
[02:18] Aisha (Security): quick security question - for private deployment we'd need KMS integration and audit logs. Do you have SOC 2 attestation?
[02:27] Lina: yes, we have SOC 2 type II, we can send the security pack. KMS integrations are supported in Private mode; hosted has managed encryption with customer-managed keys available on Dedicated/Private. We'll share the details.
[02:41] Oliver: what's the typical p95 you see for streaming with a 7B model? realistic numbers for us to budget?
[02:50] Ethan: from our benchmarks: for a 7B architecture on an optimized A100-like setup we see first-token p95 between 120-260ms for short prompts when kv cache is warm and batch sizes are small. Full-response p95 (40-80 tokens) around 600-900ms depending on parallelism and sequence length. If you run quantized on T4-like cheaper hardware numbers shift higher; Dedicated with reserved inference-optimized GPUs tends to give tighter tails.
[03:20] Noah: and tokens/sec throughput at 200 concurrent streams?
[03:24] Ethan: throughput is sensitive to per-request token rate. If you have average 10 tokens/sec per stream, 200 concurrent streams is roughly 2k tokens/sec sustained; with continuous batching we usually push higher effective throughput. Benchmarks we run include steady-state tokens/sec as well as token-latency p95. We'll propose a matrix.
[03:45] Priya: cold start behavior — how bad is cold cold? We spin up new containers frequently on surge.
[03:51] Ethan: cold starts can be noticeable for large models; for streaming we recommend warm pools or pre-warming policies. Hosted has fast warm pools for most popular model variants; Dedicated gives you always-on capacity; Private you manage warm-up but get full control.
[04:04] Maya: also routing fallback helps — if one region is congested we can failover to lower-cost variants or warm instances to keep latency under SLO.
[04:14] Oliver: about benchmarking, we want a short reproducible run using our prompt corpus, run both hosted and Dedicated-equivalent (same model) to compare p95 and token/sec cost. Can you do that with us?
[04:26] Ethan: yes, we can spin a 48-hour token/sec + p95 run. Plan: 1) get prompt set and traffic shape, 2) define candidate model variants (7B quantized, 13B compressed), 3) run parallel streams at 50/100/200 concurrency, measure first-token p95, full-response p95, 95/99 tails, and tokens/sec. We'll log traces and provide sample spans so you can subtract network overhead.
[04:53] Noah: for the Dedicated run, how closely will that map to your hosted baseline? we want apples-to-apples on hardware.
[04:59] Ethan: we'll match the GPU class as closely as possible and provide config notes: batch sizes, kernel selection, quantization flags. Hosted might use our multi-tenant pack with enhanced network paths; Dedicated will be reserved and you can get slightly better tail behavior. We'll call out differences in the report.
[05:15] Aisha: one more security — can you support SAML with SCIM for provisioning and RBAC for model access?
[05:21] Lina: yes, SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning and RBAC are supported on Dedicated and Private; hosted supports SSO with team-level controls and audit logs — we'll share the exact matrix in the security doc.
[05:33] Oliver: budget question. ballpark numbers for cost per million tokens for hosted vs dedicated reserved vs private?
[05:40] Maya: rough ranges: hosted standard for 7B quantized X-$/M tokens (we'll include exact pricing), Dedicated committed capacity has lower per-token but requires monthly commit; Private has platform fee + infra. We'll send the pricing bands and an example cost model for your 2k tokens/sec steady state and 48hr burst profile.
[06:02] Priya: curious about quantization impacts to latency — we've seen some models have slightly worse tail behavior after aggressive quantization.
[06:10] Ethan: correct, aggressive quantization can affect kernel performance and memory layout causing slightly higher variance. We'll include a quantization profile test in the matrix to capture p95 changes.
[06:22] Noah: do you capture token-level latency traces in the logs so we can debug real-time spikes?
[06:27] Lina: yes, logs include per-request token timing and we expose spans through the Console. We can also attach traces to Cloud trace providers.
[06:36] Oliver: ok, so immediate next step is the benchmark plan. We'll share sample prompts and traffic today or tomorrow.
[06:41] Maya: perfect, we'll follow up with the benchmark template and security pack. Any other blockers?
[06:47] Aisha: nothing else, just want to review security docs.
[06:50] Ethan: i'll draft the benchmark matrix after this call and include a small smoke test to validate our harness with your corpus.
[06:57] Maya: great, i'll confirm the follow-up meeting for the first week of november. Thanks everyone.
